title: The Summer London Almost Fled Parliament #Shorts

hook.narration: In eighteen fifty-eight, London smelled so bad that Parliament nearly fled.

visuals.prompt: The Houses of Parliament beside a sickly green fog rising from the Thames, Victorian London, 1858

scenes.narration: Raw sewage had poured into the Thames for years, and a hot summer cooked it.

visuals.prompt: A foul brown River Thames at low tide with sludge along the banks under a blazing hot sun, Victorian boats
Victorian Londoners covering their noses with handkerchiefs on a bridge

scenes.narration: Officials hung chemical-soaked curtains over the windows of Parliament. People believed bad air caused disease, so panic spread.

visuals.prompt: Tall Victorian Parliament windows hung with heavy white curtains soaked in chemicals, men in frock coats coughing
A worried crowd gathered near a Victorian doctor's notice about disease, gaslight

scenes.narration: Within weeks, Parliament approved a huge sewer project led by engineer Joseph Bazalgette.

visuals.prompt: A Victorian engineer unrolling large sewer blueprints on a drafting table, brass instruments, candlelight
Politicians in a packed Victorian House of Commons raising hands in a vote

scenes.narration: His tunnels still carry London's waste today.

visuals.prompt: A vast arched Victorian brick sewer tunnel stretching into darkness, water gleaming

description: The Great Stink of 1858 forced London to build a new sewer system. Here is how a smell changed a city. #Shorts #History #London

thumbnail.prompt: Westminster and the Thames under a sickly green haze at dusk, Victorian London, dramatic
